# Produce newsletters: Slack for newsletters

**Pattern:** Content Generation · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers newsletters work end to end across Slack, Airtable and WordPress.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Stamp & Shape Draft
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Build the Brief
6. Draft with AI Writer
7. OpenRouter Writer Model
8. Refine with AI Editor
9. OpenRouter Editor Model
10. Convert to HTML
11. Publish Draft to WordPress
12. Sort Drafts Newest First
13. Guard Non-Empty topic
14. Stamp Processing Time
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (Airtable)
17. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing newsletters work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Stamp & Shape Draft → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Build the Brief → Draft with AI Writer → OpenRouter Writer Model → Refine with AI Editor → OpenRouter Editor Model → Convert to HTML → Publish Draft to WordPress → Sort Drafts Newest First → Guard Non-Empty topic → Stamp Processing Time → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Airtable) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Airtable aligned by hand for newsletters
- Newsletters work where "Stamp & Shape Draft" is still a manual step before Slack
- Newsletters work that only reaches Slack on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Airtable in step for newsletters, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Slack or Airtable call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this newsletters build
- The newsletters AI step is isolated from Slack, so models swap without touching the other 19 nodes
- Fans the same result out to WordPress in the same run, for newsletters
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 19 nodes for newsletters before wiring Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; OpenRouter API key; Slack OAuth2; WordPress credentials.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Two LLM calls, not one, because a model grading its own output rarely catches its own mistakes — a dedicated critic pass, with a different system prompt focused on gaps and tone rather than generation, catches what a single writing pass misses. Publishing lands as a **draft**, never live, so a human stays the final gate before AI-authored content goes public.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Swap the Editor Model to a different provider than the Writer Model and compare the critique quality.
2. Change the critic's system message to focus on one specific weakness, like SEO or tone.
3. Add a third pass — a fact-check chain — between the writer and the editor.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**OpenRouter API key**
openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.
_Gotcha:_ One key reaches many models — handy for fallback.

**WordPress credentials**
WordPress → Users → Profile → Application Passwords → add new.
_Gotcha:_ Requires HTTPS. The regular login password will not work.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your newsletters process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- WordPress: an application password for a user with author rights, not an administrator account.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole newsletters payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
